narratives.Description: docs+doctor: guide consumers when corporate npm mirrors lag public @deftai/directive
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Corporate / mirrored npm registries (Artifactory, Nexus, Verdaccio, Azure Artifacts, etc.) can serve a stale packument for `@deftai/directive` while the package is already published on the public registry. Consumers then see `E404` / `ETARGET` for a real version, or worse — `@latest` silently installs an older version (e.g. mirror stuck at `0.80.0` while public is `0.84.0`).

This is not a missing publish. Directive already pins its own release probes to `https://registry.npmjs.org/` (session release-availability / staleness tickler), but **consumer install/upgrade commands** (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`) honor the user's configured registry. Docs do not mention this failure mode today, and `deft doctor` does not steer operators toward the fix.

### Field evidence (2026-07-24)

Consumer on macOS with:

```text
npm config get registry
→ https://cfa.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/npm/npm/

npm view @deftai/directive version
→ 0.80.0

npm view @deftai/directive@0.84.0 version
→ E404 No match found for version 0.84.0

npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.84.0
→ ETARGET No matching version found
```

Public registry at the same time: `@deftai/directive@0.84.0` (and siblings) all present; `latest` = `0.84.0`.

## Goals

Ship **both**:

1. **Docs** — UPGRADING notes (+ thin README pointer) so humans/agents can diagnose and unblock.
2. **Doctor** — an advisory finding that detects a non-public / mirrored default registry (or a related install mismatch) and points the operator at those UPGRADING notes.

## Scope A — Docs

### `content/UPGRADING.md`

Add a short callout near **Canonical upgrade — npm**, e.g. "Corporate / mirrored npm registry", covering:

- Symptoms: `E404` / `ETARGET` for a version that exists on the GitHub release; or `@latest` resolving older than the published release
- Diagnosis: `npm config get registry` — if not `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, you are on a mirror
- Unblock (one-shot): `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<ver> --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`
- Durable: `@deftai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` in user/project `.npmrc` (keep company default for other scopes)
- Org fix: re-cache / remote-sync **all four** packages — `@deftai/directive`, `directive-core`, `directive-content`, `directive-types`
- Silent-stale warning: `@latest` can succeed on an outdated mirror

### `README.md`

One sentence in the cold-start / install area (sibling to the existing Offline tip) linking into that UPGRADING section. Keep README thin.

## Scope B — Doctor

Add an advisory doctor finding (prefer **offline-capable**) that:

1. Reads the effective npm registry (`npm config get registry` or equivalent seam) without contacting any registry by default.
2. When the configured registry is **not** the public npm registry (`https://registry.npmjs.org/` / trailing-slash normalized), emits a non-blocking advisory whose remediation text **links/points to the new UPGRADING section** (path + anchor), with the one-shot `--registry=` unblock and the scoped `.npmrc` option.
3. Remains compatible with `content/tools/package-manager-network.md`: bare `deft doctor` stays offline; no new default-network contact. Optional enrichment under `deft doctor --network` is fine (e.g. if public latest and configured-registry latest diverge), but the baseline advisory must not require `--network`.
4. Does **not** tell consumers to change their org-wide default registry; only documents scoped override / one-shot / IT sync.

Suggested finding identity (bikeshed OK): `npm-registry-mirror` or `configured-npm-registry`.

## Non-goals

- Second install channel or publishing to Artifactory ourselves
- Auto-rewriting consumer `.npmrc`
- Treating mirrored registries as an error that fails doctor closed
- Changing the canonical SoT away from public npm

## Acceptance

- [ ] UPGRADING section merged with symptoms, diagnosis, one-shot unblock, scoped override, sibling-package sync note, silent-stale warning
- [ ] README one-liner points at that section
- [ ] `deft doctor` (offline tier) surfaces the advisory when default registry ≠ public npmjs and points at the UPGRADING section
- [ ] Tests for the doctor finding (public registry → no advisory; mirrored registry → advisory + UPGRADING pointer)
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` note (docs + doctor)

## Related

- `content/tools/package-manager-network.md` — doctor offline-by-default contract
- `packages/core/src/session/release-availability.ts` / `staleness-tickler/probe-directive.ts` — already force `--registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`
- Informational remote-version probe precedent (#801)


---

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-07-24T15:55:36Z)

## Proposed implementation (approved 2026-07-24)

The issue is reproducible: the configured JFrog registry resolves `@deftai/directive` to `0.80.0`, while the public npm registry resolves `@deftai/directive` and its three sibling packages to `0.84.0`.

### Design amendments

1. **Resolve the effective registry for the `@deftai` scope.**
   - Query `npm config get @deftai:registry` first.
   - When unset (`undefined` / empty), fall back to `npm config get registry`.
   - This prevents a false-positive after the documented scoped override is applied.

2. **Keep the baseline check offline and advisory-only.**
   - The only subprocesses are local `npm config get ...` reads, run in the consumer project root with a timeout and no shell.
   - A non-public effective registry emits warning finding `npm-registry-mirror` but never changes the doctor exit code.
   - Unavailable/malformed npm config output degrades to a non-warning skip.
   - Do not render the raw configured URL in text or JSON; it may contain credentials or disclose an internal hostname.

3. **Cover normal and throttle-skipped doctor paths.**
   - Run the advisory in the full doctor path.
   - Include it in the lightweight local signposts evaluated when doctor is throttle-skipped, so a registry configuration change is not hidden for up to 24 hours.

4. **Correct the existing network-tier probe.**
   - `packages/core/src/doctor/payload-staleness.ts` currently runs `npm view` without a registry override even though doctor discloses `registry.npmjs.org`.
   - Add `--registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` and `--ignore-scripts` so `deft doctor --network` compares against the public source of truth.

5. **Documentation.**
   - Add stable heading `### Corporate or mirrored npm registry` under the canonical npm upgrade section.
   - Cover `E404` / `ETARGET`, silently stale `@latest`, diagnosis, one-shot public-registry install, scoped `.npmrc` override, and organization mirror synchronization.
   - Use the complete package names: `@deftai/directive`, `@deftai/directive-core`, `@deftai/directive-content`, and `@deftai/directive-types`.
   - State that bypassing the corporate mirror is only appropriate where organization policy permits; otherwise request an IT-side sync.
   - Add a thin README cold-start pointer and update `content/tools/package-manager-network.md` to distinguish offline-safe `npm config get` from network-reaching `npm view`.

### Test matrix

- public default registry -> no warning
- mirrored default registry -> advisory + UPGRADING pointer
- public `@deftai:registry` with mirrored default -> no warning
- mirrored scoped registry with public default -> advisory
- npm unavailable / malformed output -> skip, never fail doctor
- raw registry credentials/internal URL never rendered
- throttle-skipped doctor still emits the advisory
- baseline doctor invokes no network-capable npm/git command
- `doctor --network` pins `npm view` to public npm
- advisory remains exit-code 0
- README/UPGRADING content-contract coverage plus CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`

Implementation will use a dedicated tested doctor module, an injected npm-config runner seam, and the existing finding/output contracts.
